newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The number of defaulters on bond repayments has dropped sharply to 35,000 from 49,000 last yer, Mortgage Indemnity Fund figures show.

- The SA Revenue Service is planning to introduce two systems to boost personal and company tax collection and customs income, after estimating that 95 percent of all imported produce falls within the technical definition of "smuggled goods".
- Employees of privatised parastatals would be given the right to buy shares worth 10,000 rand in their companies at a discount, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday.

- South African Cricket captain Hansie Cronje, rather than taking satisfaction from a wicket at a crucial late stage on Monday's fightback in the second test in Port Elizabeth, could think only of the ball that allowed Ian Healy to hit the six than won the game for Australia.

- A consortium made up of investment groups Siphumelele and IPG, and women's investment group Nozala, are set to conclude a deal this week with one of SA's biggest catering companies, Fedics, to acquire 33 percent of its equity for 400 million rand.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Christo Nel, the Transkei attorney general, has issued a warrant for the arrest of David Bloomberg, former Cape Town mayor and lawyer, and associate of hotel magnate Sol Kerzner.

- The South African Rail Computer Corporation, the loss-making state commuter service, would not act to eliminate fare evasion even though this could cost as much as 30 percent of its fare income, the parastatal said on Monday.

- The number of trades on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange reached a new record on Monday of 15,418, twenty five percent above the previous record of 12,354, as the March futures close-out caused frantic activity.

- Despite a strong performance in all its other operating companies, Anglo American Industrial Corporation (Amic) has failed to offset the losses at Columbus Stainless Steel and lower profits at Mondi.
SAKE BEELD
- South Africa's second tax-amnesty that expired last month, was particularly successful. It returned almost 1 billion rand in unpaid taxes to the state.
- Anglo American Industrial Corporation (Amic) is aiming for real growth in earnings in the year ahead after a poor performance last year.
- The sale of thirty percent of Telkom will bring in income of seven billion rand for the government, Minister of Public Enterprise, Stella Sigcau said on Monday.
THE STAR

- Former activist Dr Allan Boesak has been accused of "cheap politicking" for claiming that his conviction on fraud and theft charges would amount to the conviction of the entire anti-apartheid struggle.

- The grass was green and damp from overnight rains. The sunflowers bloomed. The sun obliged. The white-stone building that is the official residence of South Africa's first citizen glowed as staff members, policemen and the media gathered to get a glimpse of his guest, Princess Diana.
- Anti-corruption and South African Police Services Special Task Force members raided eight illegal casinos last night after a two-month investigation.

- In what has been billed as one of the most important media appointments this year, Cape Argus editor Shaun Johnson is set to become group ediorial director of Independent Newspapers, the country's largest newspaper group.
